title: Leather for the earth
hook: you can't answer every bad take online; Shantideva can't pave the earth in leather, but he can wear sandals
tomorrow: anger is rising and the words are coming. what does a log do?

segments.voice: Yesterday's teaching, guard the mind: one watchful guard keeps every rule on the list. Today shows why that guard is enough, with a pair of sandals.

Somewhere online, right now, someone is wrong. A bad take, a rude comment, a stranger misunderstanding something you care about. You could answer every one of them. People try. It never ends, because there's always another. Shantideva had his own version of the problem, and his answer is a picture you can stand in, quite literally.
screen: `SOMEONE ONLINE IS WRONG.` → `ANSWER EVERY ONE?` → `IT NEVER ENDS.`

segments.voice: Difficult people, he says, are as endless as space; you could never overcome them all. Then the picture. Where would you find enough leather to cover the whole earth, so the stones and thorns never hurt your feet? Nowhere. But put leather on the soles of your own feet, and it's as if the whole earth were covered. So with the world, he says: I can't hold back everything outside, but I can hold back my own mind. That's the guard from yesterday, given shoes. Now the week, in six lines. Guard the vow: a promise is a flame you cup. No hands, no feet: craving borrows yours. They can go: ancient isn't forever. Stand firm: feet down, don't bow. Where would it live: look, and the urge has no home. Guard the mind: one guard keeps them all. And today, the one that makes the rest walkable. Leather on your feet.
screen: `ENDLESS AS SPACE.` · `NO LEATHER FOR THE WHOLE EARTH.` · `HOLD BACK YOUR OWN MIND.` · `SIX LINES FROM THE WEEK.` · then, large: `LEATHER ON YOUR FEET.`

segments.voice: Stand up and walk slowly for about a minute, indoors or out, shoes or bare feet. Feel each sole meet the ground: heel, the outer edge, the toes. Every step lands on something you didn't choose and can't smooth out, and your feet carry you anyway.
Leather for the earth: Shantideva's sandal picture. You can't cover the world, so you guard where you stand.
The line for this one: leather on your feet, not on the whole earth. A week of Shantideva on care and watchfulness, done.

screen: `DAY 1477 COUNTS.` → `SHANTIDEVA'S GUIDE · 22 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: ANGER IS RISING AND THE WORDS ARE COMING. WHAT DOES A LOG DO?`

howItsDone: Tibetan and other Mahayana teachers often quote Shantideva's leather verse when teaching that practice works on one's own reactions rather than on changing everyone around.

myth: the leather verse says the world's problems don't matter

fork.setup: a group chat keeps sharing jokes that sting you a little. you can't control what they post. what's the leather-on-your-feet move?
options: reply to every joke until they finally see your side.
work on how you meet the jokes: notice the sting, choose your reply.
leave every group chat, so nothing can sting again.
fork.reveal: you can't pave the earth. Shantideva guards the one place he stands: his own mind. speaking up is still allowed, from a guarded mind.

original.note: Sanskrit: mind, heart; what Shantideva guards in chapter five. Pali citta.

what a scholar hears: the verse follows 'beings are endless as space' and closes with restraining one's own mind; it's a key image for chapter five's guarding.
guess: guarding your own mind instead of trying to fix the world
a gift of sandals given to traveling monks long ago
covering the ground so nobody ever gets hurt again

chat.says: kids keep walking past the mural with opinions. 'make it brighter.' 'why a crane?' can't make them all stop.
options: You can't. Guard how you meet them instead: hear it, keep what helps, keep painting.
Put up a sign asking everyone to keep their opinions to themselves till it's done.
Change the mural each time, so every single person ends up liking it.
chat.meaning: No leather covers the whole earth; leather on your feet does. Shantideva guards his own mind, not every passerby.

Shantideva.meaning: Buddhist poet-monk who wrote this guide to the bodhisattva's way

craving.meaning: the thirsty pull toward more; a root of suffering in Buddhism

vow.meaning: here, the bodhisattva's promise to wake up for all beings

sources.ref: Bodhicaryavatara 5.12-5.14 (unruly beings are endless as space; no leather to cover the earth, but leather on the soles covers it; I cannot restrain external things, but I will restrain my mind)
